Prize share: 1/1

# Marie Curie

## Facts

![Image 3: Nobel Prizes 2026](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_27])

Photo from the Nobel Foundation archive.

Marie Curie, née Skłodowska

 Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1911

Born: 7 November 1867, Warsaw, Russian Empire (now Poland)

Died: 4 July 1934, Sallanches, France

Affiliation at the time of the award: Sorbonne University, Paris, France

Prize motivation: “in recognition of her services to the advancement of chemistry by the discovery of the elements radium and polonium, by the isolation of radium and the study of the nature and compounds of this remarkable element”

Prize share: 1/1

Also awarded: [Nobel Prize in Physics 1903](link_28)

### Life

Marie Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, Poland, to a family of teachers who believed strongly in education. She moved to Paris to continue her studies and there met Pierre Curie, who became both her husband and colleague in the field of radioactivity. The couple later shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics. Marie was widowed in 1906, but continued the couple's work and went on to become the first person ever to be awarded two Nobel Prizes. During World War I, Curie organized mobile X-ray teams. The Curies' daughter, Irene, was also jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside her husband, Frederic Joliot

### Work

After Marie Skłodowska Curie and Pierre Curie first discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium, Marie continued to investigate their properties. In 1910 she successfully produced radium as a pure metal, which proved the new element's existence beyond a doubt. She also documented the properties of the radioactive elements and their compounds. Radioactive compounds became important as sources of radiation in both scientific experiments and in the field of medicine, where they are used to treat tumors.

# Marie Curie

## Facts

![Image 3: Nobel Prizes 2026](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_27])

Photo from the Nobel Foundation archive.

Marie Curie, née Skłodowska

 Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1911

Born: 7 November 1867, Warsaw, Russian Empire (now Poland)

Died: 4 July 1934, Sallanches, France

Affiliation at the time of the award: Sorbonne University, Paris, France

Prize motivation: “in recognition of her services to the advancement of chemistry by the discovery of the elements radium and polonium, by the isolation of radium and the study of the nature and compounds of this remarkable element”

Prize share: 1/1

Also awarded: [Nobel Prize in Physics 1903](link_28)

### Life

Marie Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, Poland, to a family of teachers who believed strongly in education. She moved to Paris to continue her studies and there met Pierre Curie, who became both her husband and colleague in the field of radioactivity. The couple later shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics. Marie was widowed in 1906, but continued the couple's work and went on to become the first person ever to be awarded two Nobel Prizes. During World War I, Curie organized mobile X-ray teams. The Curies' daughter, Irene, was also jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside her husband, Frederic Joliot

### Work

After Marie Skłodowska Curie and Pierre Curie first discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium, Marie continued to investigate their properties. In 1910 she successfully produced radium as a pure metal, which proved the new element's existence beyond a doubt. She also documented the properties of the radioactive elements and their compounds. Radioactive compounds became important as sources of radiation in both scientific experiments and in the field of medicine, where they are used to treat tumors.

Physics

### [Ice at the South Pole reveals cosmic particle accelerators](link_16)

[Francis Halzen](link_18)‘s vision and scientific leadership have been fundamental for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory – a cubic kilometre of ice that is equipped with light sensors.

[![Image 20: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/press-release/ [link_16])

Chemistry

### [They made chemistry choose a mirror image](link_20)

For a long time, chemists wondered how homochirality can emerge.[Henri B. Kagan](link_22) and [Kenso Soai](link_24)found a solution to this puzzle.

[![Image 22: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/press-release/ [link_20])

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

Medicine

### [Light-seeking algae gave us a switch for nerve cells](link_25)

[Karl Deisseroth](link_27), [Peter Hegemann](link_29) and [Georg Nagel](link_31) made discoveries leading to optogenetics, which makes it possible to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells in a living brain.

[![Image 24: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/press-release/ [link_25])

© The Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine. Ill. Mattias Karlén

Literature

### [Anne Carson](link_32)

The literature prize was awarded to the Canadian author [Anne Carson](link_34) “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature.”

[![Image 26: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/2026/press-release/ [link_32])

Ill. Niklas Elmehed © Nobel Prize Outreach

Peace

### [Navanethem “Navi” Pillay](link_35)

[Navi Pillay](link_37) has been at the forefront in the development of an international legal order.She has held states and national leaders accountable and brought hope to victims of violence and conflict.

[![Image 28: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2026/press-release/ [link_35])

Ill. Niklas Elmehed © Nobel Prize Outreach

Economic sciences

### [Microfoundations deliver macro insights](link_38)

[Robert E. Hall](link_40)’s and [Michael Woodford](link_42)’s research has generated a paradigm shift in stabilisation policy.

[![Image 30: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2026/press-release/ [link_38])

Physics

### [Ice at the South Pole reveals cosmic particle accelerators](link_16)

[Francis Halzen](link_18)‘s vision and scientific leadership have been fundamental for the IceCube Neutrino Observatory – a cubic kilometre of ice that is equipped with light sensors.

[![Image 20: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2026/press-release/ [link_16])

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

Chemistry

### [They made chemistry choose a mirror image](link_20)

For a long time, chemists wondered how homochirality can emerge.[Henri B. Kagan](link_22) and [Kenso Soai](link_24)found a solution to this puzzle.

[![Image 22: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2026/press-release/ [link_20])

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

Medicine

### [Light-seeking algae gave us a switch for nerve cells](link_25)

[Karl Deisseroth](link_27), [Peter Hegemann](link_29) and [Georg Nagel](link_31) made discoveries leading to optogenetics, which makes it possible to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells in a living brain.

[![Image 24: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/2026/press-release/ [link_25])

© The Nobel Committee for Physiology or Medicine. Ill. Mattias Karlén

Literature

### [Anne Carson](link_32)

The literature prize was awarded to the Canadian author [Anne Carson](link_34) “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature.”

[![Image 26: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/literature/2026/press-release/ [link_32])

Ill. Niklas Elmehed © Nobel Prize Outreach

Peace

### [Navanethem “Navi” Pillay](link_35)

[Navi Pillay](link_37) has been at the forefront in the development of an international legal order.She has held states and national leaders accountable and brought hope to victims of violence and conflict.

[![Image 28: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/peace/2026/press-release/ [link_35])

Ill. Niklas Elmehed © Nobel Prize Outreach

Economic sciences

### [Microfoundations deliver macro insights](link_38)

[Robert E. Hall](link_40)’s and [Michael Woodford](link_42)’s research has generated a paradigm shift in stabilisation policy.

[![Image 30: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/economic-sciences/2026/press-release/ [link_38])

© Johan Jarnestad/The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences

 An educational resource about this year’s Nobel Prize laureates and their groundbreaking work. 

[Explore the lessons](link_43)

 Economic sciences 
### [“They’re probably hoping I’ll cancel the exam”](link_44)

 Michael Woodford was scheduled to be setting his economics students an exam on the morning, when he was woken by a call from Stockholm. 

![Image 32: Susumu Tonegawa](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_19])

*    Peace

# Marie Curie
## Facts
![Image 3: Nobel Prizes 2026](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)
Photo from the Nobel Foundation archive.
Marie Curie, née Skłodowska
Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1911
Born: 7 November 1867, Warsaw, Russian Empire (now Poland)
Died: 4 July 1934, Sallanches, France
Affiliation at the time of the award: Sorbonne University, Paris, France
Prize motivation: “in recognition of her services to the advancement of chemistry by the discovery of the elements radium and polonium, by the isolation of radium and the study of the nature and compounds of this remarkable element”
Prize share: 1/1
Also awarded: [Nobel Prize in Physics 1903](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/summary/)

# Marie Curie
## Facts
### Life
Marie Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, Poland, to a family of teachers who believed strongly in education. She moved to Paris to continue her studies and there met Pierre Curie, who became both her husband and colleague in the field of radioactivity. The couple later shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics. Marie was widowed in 1906, but continued the couple's work and went on to become the first person ever to be awarded two Nobel Prizes. During World War I, Curie organized mobile X-ray teams. The Curies' daughter, Irene, was also jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside her husband, Frederic Joliot

# Marie Curie
## Facts
### Work
After Marie Skłodowska Curie and Pierre Curie first discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium, Marie continued to investigate their properties. In 1910 she successfully produced radium as a pure metal, which proved the new element's existence beyond a doubt. She also documented the properties of the radioactive elements and their compounds. Radioactive compounds became important as sources of radiation in both scientific experiments and in the field of medicine, where they are used to treat tumors.

# Marie Curie
## Facts
![Image 3: Nobel Prizes 2026](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)

Marie Curie, née Skłodowska
Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1911
Born: 7 November 1867, Warsaw, Russian Empire (now Poland)
Died: 4 July 1934, Sallanches, France
Affiliation at the time of the award: Sorbonne University, Paris, France
Prize motivation: “in recognition of her services to the advancement of chemistry by the discovery of the elements radium and polonium, by the isolation of radium and the study of the nature and compounds of this remarkable element”
Prize share: 1/1
Also awarded: [Nobel Prize in Physics 1903](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/summary/)

# Marie Curie
## Facts
### Life
Marie Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, Poland, to a family of teachers who believed strongly in education. She moved to Paris to continue her studies and there met Pierre Curie, who became both her husband and colleague in the field of radioactivity. The couple later shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics. Marie was widowed in 1906, but continued the couple's work and went on to become the first person ever to be awarded two Nobel Prizes. During World War I, Curie organized mobile X-ray teams. The Curies' daughter, Irene, was also jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside her husband, Frederic Joliot

# Marie Curie
## Facts
### Work
After Marie Skłodowska Curie and Pierre Curie first discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium, Marie continued to investigate their properties. In 1910 she successfully produced radium as a pure metal, which proved the new element's existence beyond a doubt. She also documented the properties of the radioactive elements and their compounds. Radioactive compounds became important as sources of radiation in both scientific experiments and in the field of medicine, where they are used to treat tumors.

# Marie Curie
## Facts
### Life
Marie Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, Poland, to a family of teachers who believed strongly in education. She moved to Paris to continue her studies and there met Pierre Curie, who became both her husband and colleague in the field of radioactivity. The couple later shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics. Marie was widowed in 1906, but continued the couple's work and went on to become the first person ever to be awarded two Nobel Prizes. During World War I, Curie organized mobile X-ray teams. The Curies' daughter, Irene, was also jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside her husband, Frederic Joliot

# Marie Curie
## Facts
### Life
Marie Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, Poland, to a family of teachers who believed strongly in education. She moved to Paris to continue her studies and there met Pierre Curie, who became both her husband and colleague in the field of radioactivity. The couple later shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics. Marie was widowed in 1906, but continued the couple's work and went on to become the first person ever to be awarded two Nobel Prizes. During World War I, Curie organized mobile X-ray teams. The Curies' daughter, Irene, was also jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside her husband, Frederic Joliot

# Marie Curie
## Facts
![Image 3: Nobel Prizes 2026](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)
Photo from the Nobel Foundation archive.
Marie Curie, née Skłodowska
Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1911
Born: 7 November 1867, Warsaw, Russian Empire (now Poland)
Died: 4 July 1934, Sallanches, France
Affiliation at the time of the award: Sorbonne University, Paris, France
Prize motivation: “in recognition of her services to the advancement of chemistry by the discovery of the elements radium and polonium, by the isolation of radium and the study of the nature and compounds of this remarkable element”
Prize share: 1/1
Also awarded: [Nobel Prize in Physics 1903](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/summary/)
state.next_chunk:
# Marie Curie
## Facts
### Work
After Marie Skłodowska Curie and Pierre Curie first discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium, Marie continued to investigate their properties. In 1910 she successfully produced radium as a pure metal, which proved the new element's existence beyond a doubt. She also documented the properties of the radioactive elements and their compounds. Radioactive compounds became important as sources of radiation in both scientific experiments and in the field of medicine, where they are used to treat tumors.

# Marie Curie

## Facts

![Image 3: Nobel Prizes 2026](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_27])

Photo from the Nobel Foundation archive.

Marie Curie, née Skłodowska

 Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1911

Born: 7 November 1867, Warsaw, Russian Empire (now Poland)

Died: 4 July 1934, Sallanches, France

Affiliation at the time of the award: Sorbonne University, Paris, France

Prize motivation: “in recognition of her services to the advancement of chemistry by the discovery of the elements radium and polonium, by the isolation of radium and the study of the nature and compounds of this remarkable element”

Prize share: 1/1

Also awarded: [Nobel Prize in Physics 1903](link_28)

### Life

Marie Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, Poland, to a family of teachers who believed strongly in education. She moved to Paris to continue her studies and there met Pierre Curie, who became both her husband and colleague in the field of radioactivity. The couple later shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics. Marie was widowed in 1906, but continued the couple's work and went on to become the first person ever to be awarded two Nobel Prizes. During World War I, Curie organized mobile X-ray teams. The Curies' daughter, Irene, was also jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside her husband, Frederic Joliot

### Work

After Marie Skłodowska Curie and Pierre Curie first discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium, Marie continued to investigate their properties. In 1910 she successfully produced radium as a pure metal, which proved the new element's existence beyond a doubt. She also documented the properties of the radioactive elements and their compounds. Radioactive compounds became important as sources of radiation in both scientific experiments and in the field of medicine, where they are used to treat tumors.

# Marie Curie

## Facts

![Image 3: Nobel Prizes 2026](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1 [link_27])

Photo from the Nobel Foundation archive.

Marie Curie, née Skłodowska

 Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1911

Born: 7 November 1867, Warsaw, Russian Empire (now Poland)

Died: 4 July 1934, Sallanches, France

Affiliation at the time of the award: Sorbonne University, Paris, France

Prize motivation: “in recognition of her services to the advancement of chemistry by the discovery of the elements radium and polonium, by the isolation of radium and the study of the nature and compounds of this remarkable element”

Prize share: 1/1

Also awarded: [Nobel Prize in Physics 1903](link_28)

### Life

Marie Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, Poland, to a family of teachers who believed strongly in education. She moved to Paris to continue her studies and there met Pierre Curie, who became both her husband and colleague in the field of radioactivity. The couple later shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics. Marie was widowed in 1906, but continued the couple's work and went on to become the first person ever to be awarded two Nobel Prizes. During World War I, Curie organized mobile X-ray teams. The Curies' daughter, Irene, was also jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside her husband, Frederic Joliot

### Work

After Marie Skłodowska Curie and Pierre Curie first discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium, Marie continued to investigate their properties. In 1910 she successfully produced radium as a pure metal, which proved the new element's existence beyond a doubt. She also documented the properties of the radioactive elements and their compounds. Radioactive compounds became important as sources of radiation in both scientific experiments and in the field of medicine, where they are used to treat tumors.

# Marie Curie
## Facts
![Image 3: Nobel Prizes 2026](blob:http://localhost/aef335eb562a1da6957ce25a574b4aa1)
Photo from the Nobel Foundation archive.
Marie Curie, née Skłodowska
Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1911
Born: 7 November 1867, Warsaw, Russian Empire (now Poland)
Died: 4 July 1934, Sallanches, France
Affiliation at the time of the award: Sorbonne University, Paris, France
Prize motivation: “in recognition of her services to the advancement of chemistry by the discovery of the elements radium and polonium, by the isolation of radium and the study of the nature and compounds of this remarkable element”
Prize share: 1/1
Also awarded: [Nobel Prize in Physics 1903](https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/1903/summary/)

# Marie Curie
## Facts
### Life
Marie Skłodowska was born in Warsaw, Poland, to a family of teachers who believed strongly in education. She moved to Paris to continue her studies and there met Pierre Curie, who became both her husband and colleague in the field of radioactivity. The couple later shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics. Marie was widowed in 1906, but continued the couple's work and went on to become the first person ever to be awarded two Nobel Prizes. During World War I, Curie organized mobile X-ray teams. The Curies' daughter, Irene, was also jointly awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside her husband, Frederic Joliot

# Marie Curie
## Facts
### Work
After Marie Skłodowska Curie and Pierre Curie first discovered the radioactive elements polonium and radium, Marie continued to investigate their properties. In 1910 she successfully produced radium as a pure metal, which proved the new element's existence beyond a doubt. She also documented the properties of the radioactive elements and their compounds. Radioactive compounds became important as sources of radiation in both scientific experiments and in the field of medicine, where they are used to treat tumors.
